sanskrit: yat ta ātman tanvāṃ ghoram asti yad vā keśeṣu praticakṣaṇe vā | tat te vidvān apa bādhe ahaṃ pra tvā suvāt savitā saubhagāya ||
english: Whatever is dreadful in your self, in your body, or in your hair, or in your appearance — that I, knowing it, drive away from you; may Savitṛ impel you forward unto good fortune.

sanskrit: nir lakṣmyaṃ lalāmyaṃ nir arātiṃ suvāmasi | yathā no vasyasīd aso rāyaspoṣam ihā suva ||
english: We impel out the ill-omened mark, the evil sign, and hostility — so that you may be more prosperous for us; impel here the swelling of riches.

sanskrit: agnim accha devayatāṃ manāṃsi cakṣūṃṣīva sūryaṃ saṃ caranti | yadī suvāte uṣasā virūpe śveto vājī jāyate agre ahnām ||
english: The minds of those who seek the gods stream toward Agni as eyes stream toward the Sun. When the two Dawns of differing forms set forth together, the white steed is born at the front of the days.

sanskrit: indro rājā jagataś carṣaṇīnām adhi kṣami viṣurūpaṃ yad asti | tato dadāti dāśuṣe vasūni codad rādha upastutaś cid arvāk ||
english: Indra is king of the world, of all peoples, over the earth, over whatever exists in diverse forms. From that abundance he gives treasures to the worshiper; even when praised from afar he drives generosity near.

sanskrit: śakunir bhūtvā pra babhasti pippalaṃ patyāṃ niviṣṭā yadi vā gha patnyām | bhīmā ghorā lakṣmyaḥ sahabhavyās tā ito haviṣā nir yajāmaḥ ||
english: Having become a bird it pecks the fig-tree; whether it has settled on the husband or indeed on the wife — the terrible, dreadful ill-omened portents that are companions of misfortune: those we drive away from here with an oblation.

sanskrit: yā te gṛheṣūta vā dhaneṣu prajāṃ lakṣmīr yadi vā te babhasti | tāṃ bṛhaspatir haviṣā bādhamāno nirhūya pra dadhmāv adhi dūram asmat ||
english: Whatever ill-luck in your houses or in your wealth devours your offspring, or devours you — that, as Bṛhaspati repels it with oblation and has driven it out, we blow it away far from us.

sanskrit: riśyapadīṃ riśadvatīṃ goṣedhāṃ vidhamām uta | vilīḍhyaṃ vyādhyaṃ brahmaṇā tā anīnaśam ||
english: Her of the deer's feet, the wounding one, the cow-scatterer, the extinguisher; the licker-away and the afflicting one — those I have destroyed with sacred utterance.

sanskrit: pratyoṣantīm utsaṅginīm uta cchidrām utāraṇīm | siṃhīṃ jyeṣṭhalakṣmīṃ vyāghrīṃ nāśayāmasi ||
english: The one who burns back, the one who clings, and also the one full of holes, the one who brings down; the lioness, the eldest ill-luck, the tigress — these we destroy.

sanskrit: anudhyāyinīṃ paricarāṃ vibādhām uta hiṃsatīm | rodasya patnīṃ rodhanāṃ pra tā dhamāmi lakṣmyaḥ ||
english: The brooding one, the roaming one, the obstructress, and also the harming one; the wife of Rodas, the one who blocks — those ill-omens I blow away.

sanskrit: vāmaspṛhāṃ pitṛṣadaṃ yeṣantīṃ tapanīm uta | asidhyantīṃ pradhvaṃsinīm aṣṭrāvadhāṃ ca lakṣmyaṃ brahmaṇā tā anīnaśam ||
english: The one who craves the left, the one who sits with the ancestors, the one who stirs about, and also the scorching one; the one who fails to succeed, the destroyer, and the ill-luck that kills with a goad — those I have annihilated with the sacred utterance.

sanskrit: āsanmantryāṃ vacasyāṃ saṃpibantīṃ nyakvarīm | uttarāṃ janaṃgamāṃ pra tā dhamāmi lakṣmyaḥ ||
english: The one who whispers while seated, the chattering one, the one who drinks together, the downward-pressing one; the superior one, the one who drives people away — those ill-omens I blow away.

sanskrit: yā te ghorā tanvam āviveśa yā te lakṣmīḥ sarvā samaktā | agniṣ ṭe tāsv adatta saubhagāy- -āpaḥ śundhantu bṛhate raṇāya ||
english: Whatever dreadful ill-luck has entered your body, whatever ill-omens are all united in you — Agni has given you protection among them for good fortune; may the waters purify you for great combat.

sanskrit: adevṛghnīṃ varuṇ- -āpatighnīṃ bṛhaspate | indrāputraghnīṃ lakṣmyam asyai tāḥ savitaḥ suva ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, the ill-luck that does not kill a brother-in-law, Varuṇa — the one that kills a husband; O Savitṛ, impel away from her those ill-omens that kill the sons of Indra.

sanskrit: yā te lakṣmīś cakṣuṣi yota datsu yā hastayo stanayor yopapakṣayoḥ | śroṇyor bhaṃsasi yā padoṣ ṭe sarvās tā ati krāma ghorāḥ ||
english: Whatever ill-luck is in your eyes, or in your teeth, or in your hands, in your breasts, or in your armpits; in your hips, in your buttocks, or in your feet — step beyond all those dreadful ones.

sanskrit: ūrubhyāṃ te aṣṭhīvadbhyāṃ pārṣṇibhyāṃ prapadābhyām | lakṣmīḥ śroṇibhyām aṅgebhyo yāḥ pāpīs tā anīnaśan ||
english: From your thighs, from your kneecaps, from your heels, from the balls of your feet; the ill-omens from your hips, from your limbs — those sinful ones they have destroyed.

sanskrit: apāślīlaṃ pṛthivī hantu yat pador apa hastayor varuṇo mitro aryamā | apādityā anumatī rarāṇāḥ pra ṇaḥ suvāt savitā saubhagāya ||
english: May the earth smite away the obscenity that is in the feet, away from the hands — Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman; the Ādityas, Anumati, taking delight — may Savitṛ impel us forward unto good fortune.

sanskrit: etā enā vyākaran khile gā aditīr iva | ramantāṃ bhadrā lakṣmyo yāḥ pāpīs tā anīnaśan ||
english: They have driven apart these two, the cows in the barren patch, like Aditīs. May the auspicious good fortunes take delight; those that are sinful — they have been annihilated.

sanskrit: sāhuṣī nāma vā asi sahamānā sahasvatī | gṛhaguptim anuvartiṃ kulāyinīṃ tā ihā veśayāmasi ||
english: You are indeed named Sāhuṣī — the all-conquering, the mighty-possessing one; the guardian of the house, the follower, the nest-maker — those we install here.

sanskrit: ?saṃcāriṇy ubhair yā babhūv- -ānyā anyāṃ jinvati bhadrapāpīḥ | tāṃ lakṣmīṃ nihavā nayāmo bhadrā subhadrām api saubhagāya? ||
english: She who has come to pass on both sides, who moves about — one quickens the other, auspicious and sinful alike. That goddess of fortune we lead down by invocation; the auspicious, the very auspicious one, also for good fortune.

sanskrit: ekaśataṃ lakṣmyas tāsāṃ rājñī babhūvitha | bhadrābhir bhadre saṃbhūya bhadreṇābhi sacasva naḥ ||
english: One hundred and one are the fortune-goddesses; of those you have become queen. O auspicious one, uniting together with auspicious ones, attend to us with auspiciousness.

sanskrit: divas pṛthivyāḥ pary antarikṣād vātāt paśubhyo adhy oṣadhībhyaḥ | yato lakṣmīr vṛjinā saṃbabhūva sā brahmaṇā pracyutā dūram etu ||
english: From sky, from earth, from the atmosphere, from the wind, from cattle, and from plants — wherever the wicked ill-luck has arisen together, dislodged by the sacred utterance, may it go far away.

sanskrit: vālkutsasya ca gandhena hiraṇyavarcasena ca | āt puṣkariṇyā yo gandho bhago mā tena jinvatu ||
english: With the fragrance of the Vālkutsa plant and with the golden radiance, and with whatever fragrance belongs to the lotus pond — may Bhaga quicken me with that.

sanskrit: yad indro agre asurāñ jaghāna tato lakṣmīr ny adadhur martyeṣu | tāsāṃ pāpiṣṭhā nir ataḥ suvāmaḥ śivā asyai jātavedo ni yaccha ||
english: When Indra smote the Asuras in the beginning, therefrom they placed ill-omens among mortals. The most sinful of those we drive out from here; O Jātavedas, extend to her the auspicious ones.

sanskrit: yā tvā lakṣmīr devṛghnī yā patighnī gṛhebhyas tvā nudate yā vyāḍā | atas tvam enaso mucyamān- -ot taremāḥ srotyāḥ sapta sākam ||
english: The ill-luck that is a brother-in-law-killer, the one that is a husband-killer, the savage one that drives you from your homes — being released from that sin, may we both cross together the seven flowing streams.

sanskrit: nipiṃśantīṃ nitudantīṃ saṃpibantīṃ nyakvarīm | prabhaṅgāṃ bhrūṇaghnīṃ lakṣmīṃ brahmaṇā tā anīnaśam ||
english: The one who grinds down, the one who pricks, the one who drinks together, the one who presses down; the breaker, the embryo-slayer, the ill-luck — those I have annihilated with the sacred utterance.

sanskrit: udojiṣṭhāṃ sahasyāṃ jayantīm aparājitām | lakṣmīr yāḥ puṇyāḥ kalyāṇīs tā asyai savitaḥ suva ||
english: The victorious in rising up, the powerful, the conquering, the unconquered — the fortunes that are meritorious and auspicious: O Savitṛ, impel those toward her.

sanskrit: lakṣmyaḥ sam alapsata sam alapsata lakṣmyaḥ | ajaiṣur bhadrā lakṣmyaḥ parā pāpīr ajeṣata ||
english: The fortunes have spoken together, have spoken together, the fortunes; the auspicious fortunes have won, the sinful ones they have conquered and sent away.

sanskrit: lakṣmīṇāṃ lakṣmītame lakṣmīṇām adhipā asi | tāṃ tvāhaṃ śuddho gopsyāmi devajā hi babhūvitha ||
english: O most auspicious among the fortune-goddesses, you are the sovereign of the fortune-goddesses. Pure, I shall protect you — for you were born of the gods.

sanskrit: sabhā ca mā samitiś cāvatāṃ prajāpater duhitarau sacetasau | yena saṃgacchā upa mā sa tiṣṭhād antar vadāni hṛdaye janānām ||
english: May the assembly and the council both protect me — Prajāpati's two daughters of one mind. With whomever I go together, may that one stand by me; may I speak within the hearts of people.

sanskrit: sabhā senā samitis tvām avantu prajāpater duhitaraḥ pracetasaḥ | yena vadāny upa mā sa śikṣād antar vadāni hṛdaye janānām ||
english: May the assembly, the army, and the council protect you — the wise daughters of Prajāpati. With whomever I shall speak, may that one be instructed toward me; may I speak within the hearts of people.
